title: Resting-state EEG before and after different study methods
description: The RECAP-EEG dataset provides resting-state electroencephalography recordings from 21 neurotypical undergraduate students collected before and after different study interventions (active retrieval practice, passive review, and control conditions) at the Federal University of Paraíba, Brazil. The dataset aims to support research into the neural correlates of learning, retrieval practice, and educational neuroscience. Recordings include pre- and post-intervention resting-state EEG with eyes-open and eyes-closed blocks.
methods_description: EEG signals were recorded using a 32-channel ActiChamp system (Brain Products GmbH, Germany) with active Ag/AgCl electrodes placed according to the international 10-20 system, impedance kept below 15 kΩ, ground at Fpz. Signals were sampled at 500 Hz and filtered between 0.5 and 50 Hz. Each session lasted about nine minutes, comprising two eyes-open and two eyes-closed blocks of 2 minutes 15 seconds each, recorded before and after a study intervention (active learning with feedback, passive review, or control). Data are organized in BIDS format with .vhdr, .eeg, and .vmrk files.

funding_references.funder_name: Coordination for the Improvement of Higher Education Personnel (CAPES)
